According to the most recent on-chain snapshot, the average exchange inflow is roughly 818.3 million SHIB, up 0.97% from the previous time frame. This indicates that the average transaction sending SHIB onto exchanges has nearly reached 835 million SHIB after breaking through the 800 million-token barrier.

Total flows paint an even more cautious picture. In contrast to outflows of 174.88 billion SHIB, exchange inflows totaled 287.59 billion SHIB. At about 112.71 billion SHIB, the difference leaves the overall exchange netflow positive.

In general, positive netflow indicates that more tokens are coming into exchange-controlled wallets than going out. Although it doesn't guarantee that those tokens will be sold right away, it does increase the quantity of easily tradable supply, which could lead to selling pressure.

However, there is a crucial counterargument. The mean exchange inflows' seven-day moving average has decreased by 36.54%, indicating that the overall inflow trend is still much weaker than it was during earlier spikes. Therefore, rather than a long-term acceleration of deposits, the most recent increase may indicate a brief revival.

The token is still trading above its shorter-term moving averages, which are grouped around $0.00000500–$0.00000520, and is currently trading around $0.00000537. Nevertheless, numerous attempts have been unsuccessful in creating momentum above $0.00000550.

The declining long-term moving average around $0.00000560–$0.00000570 continues to be the biggest challenge. In order to significantly enhance its more comprehensive technical structure, SHIB must break through this region. The next significant resistance zone is $0.00000590–$0.00000620.

title: 835 Million Shiba Inu (SHIB) Hits Exchanges in 24 Hours: Inflows Break Key Barrier
